# Everything in Summon-bot, inventoried from source *and* bytecode

The reference repository's `.py` files are one snapshot of one branch; its
`__pycache__` is a snapshot of what the running bot actually had. The two disagree,
and the disagreement is where the interesting features live — character uploads among
them. This page is the raw material the port is checked against: every function in
every module, marked **lost** when it exists only in bytecode, plus the non-Python
assets the code assumes exist.

Bytecode decoding: `xdis` available.
Reference commit: `504fe36`.

## How to read this

This file is the audit trail behind every row of the table below: it says, per module of
the reference deployment, *where* that behaviour lives in this repository — or why it does
not. `scripts/extract_summon_reference.py` renders it into this document, so a module can
never be quietly forgotten: the extractor lists what the reference *has*, the map has to
account for each name in that list.

Statuses: **ported** (same behaviour, same strings) · **adapted** (same behaviour, this
repo's storage/engine conventions) · **superseded** (the reference's job is done by a
different mechanism here) · **tooling** (offline or deployment script, not bot behaviour) ·
**gap** (not implemented; see the note — a gap is recorded, not hidden).

### The one that matters most: `/upload`

`upload_character` is **not in the reference's source tree**. It exists only in the
deployment's compiled cache (`__pycache__/commands_admin.cpython-313.pyc`: `new_upload_id`,
`upload_to_catbox`, `upload_to_imgbb`, `upload_character`, `upload_callback`), while
`commands_admin.py` keeps the corpse of the feature as state plus a policy comment:

```python
# ====== TEMP STORAGE ======
PENDING_UPLOADS = {}
COUNTER = {"n": 0}

# Character uploads are URL-only. Use /add and /update with a verified
# https://files.catbox.moe/... or https://i.ibb.co/... image URL.
```

So the reference repo tells two true things at once, and this bot honours both: the retired
**upload flow** is ported verbatim from the bytecode (`/upload <name> <series> <1-18>` as a
reply to a photo/video/GIF, `up_*` callbacks, gap-filled zero-padded ids, the exact refusal
strings — see `waifu/plugins/uploads.py`), and the **current policy** it was replaced by —
verified-URL ingestion through `/add` and `/update`, allow-listed to `files.catbox.moe` and
`i.ibb.co` (`media_urls.py`) — is ported too (`/addchar`, `/media`, and the same allow-list
enforced by `waifu/tg/media.py` before anything is ever fetched). The roster still starts
empty either way: both doors are admin-only, and nothing ships a character.

### Beyond the reference (additions, not ports)

Two rows of this audit are about work that has *no* counterpart upstream, recorded here so
the table cannot be read as a claim that everything new is a port:

* **``/gate`` — the join-request quiz.** ``waifu/plugins/moderation.py`` handles
  ``chat_join_request``, an update this bot has subscribed to since the first commit and that
  nothing answered; Summon-bot predates ``createChatInviteLink(creates_join_request=True)``.
  A joiner is asked, in a DM, to pick the right character out of four drawn from *this*
  deployment's own roster (the pool is cached per group for an hour, the answer index is
  randomised, three tries, then declined with a reason). State lives in the Redis/local cache,
  so the feature needed no migration; an empty roster auto-approves rather than locking a group
  out, and so does any failure to ask.
* **The four bugs the porting exposed.** Reproducing ``plugins/profile.py`` line by line meant
  drawing the same card through this repo's own send path, which is how these surfaced and why
  each now has a test: ``_kit.mode_of`` returned ``ChatMode.HTML``, a member that has never
  existed, so every non-rich reply raised; ``Chat.is_private`` (removed in aiogram 3.7) was
  read in twelve handlers, now ``waifu/utils/chats.py``; ``Cache._key`` interpolated an un-awaited
  coroutine, so no cached read ever hit and ``invalidate`` was a no-op; and ``/profile`` passed
  the summary *dict* to ``money()``, crashing the harem row. See ``tests/test_send_paths.py``,
  ``tests/test_cache.py`` and ``tests/test_profile_card.py``.

## Port map

One row per module above. `in this repo` is a path in *this* repository, so every
claim is one `git grep` away from being checked.

| module | status | in this repo | what happened to it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `__init__` | tooling | `waifu/__init__.py` | Package marker; no behaviour to port. |
| `api` | ported | `waifu/api/server.py`, `waifu/api/auth.py`, `docs/API.md` | The deleted Flask service (only in the bytecode): read-only JSON endpoints for user/inventory/characters/market/leaderboard/streak/achievements plus the Mini-App initData HMAC check. Re-implemented on aiohttp — endpoints unchanged in shape, but the two mutating routes are POST-only and will not accept a bare ?uid= in production. |
| `auto_spawn` | ported | `waifu/plugins/spawns.py`, `waifu/services/spawn.py`, `waifu/core/jobs.py` | Timed weighted spawns, hint button, claim race. The watcher is a scheduler job instead of a while-loop task, so a restart does not lose the next spawn window; both the random and weighted pickers exist (``_pick_random_character``/``_pick_weighted_character`` -> ``spawn.pick``). |
| `bootstrap_postgres` | superseded | `waifu/db/migrations/runner.py`, `waifu/db/database.py`, `waifu/settings.py` | Postgres bootstrap + schema guard. Here that is ``python -m waifu migrate`` (a small versioned runner, ``waifu/db/migrations/runner.py``) on whatever ``DATABASE_URL`` says, and the settings validator accepts exactly the two async backends (one-file SQLite, the default, or Postgres) — which is the same 'are you sure this is the right database' guard the script implemented, moved to where a typo cannot get past startup. |
| `catch_all` | ported | `waifu/core/middlewares.py`, `waifu/plugins/moderation.py`, `waifu/plugins/spawns.py`, `waifu/db/repositories/spawns.py` | Spam limiter (SPAM_LIMIT=20), group auto-registration from live traffic, and chatter-triggered spawns. Message counting is middleware with a Redis window; group tracking writes the same ``groups`` row that ``/groupsettings`` and ``/autospan`` read. |
| `check_schema` | superseded | `waifu/__main__.py` | Offline 'does the DB match the code' check -> ``python -m waifu doctor`` (migrations applied, ladders present, roster counts, redis/poll capability). |
| `commands_admin` | ported | `waifu/plugins/uploads.py`, `waifu/plugins/characters.py`, `waifu/plugins/sudo.py`, `waifu/plugins/moderation.py`, `waifu/plugins/codes.py` | The big one: ``upload_character``/``upload_callback`` (ported word for word, from bytecode), ``add_character``/``update_character``/``delete`` -> ``/addchar`` ``/media`` ``/delchar``, ``change_chance``/``chance_list`` -> ``/setchance``/``chancelist``, ``ban``/``unban``/``warn``/``removeall`` -> moderation plugin, ``gen_code``/``redeem_code`` -> codes plugin, ``broadcast``/``save_group``/``transfer``/``removeall_callback`` -> ``/broadcast`` and group tables, ``is_sudo``/``check_sudo``/``addsudo_command`` -> sudo plugin, ``get_rarity``/``get_character_media``/``get_random_character`` -> ``waifu/db/repositories/characters.py``. |
| `commands_auction` | ported | `waifu/plugins/auctions.py`, `waifu/services/auction.py` | All 22 functions: listing, bidding, custom-bid input, pinned-message updates, the closing job, my-bids and cancel. The auction tables are migration-managed rather than created lazily by ``ensure_auction_tables``. |
| `commands_hstats` | ported | `waifu/plugins/hstats.py`, `waifu/services/hstats.py` | Per-rarity harem stats, HTML page + callback pagination, premium-gated extra views (``is_premium``/``premium_left`` -> premium plugin). |
| `commands_owner` | ported | `waifu/plugins/sudo.py`, `waifu/__main__.py` | Owner numpad panel (``get_numpad_keyboard``/``open_panel``/``ownerpanel_callback``), coin granting and ``restart_bot`` -> ``/maint`` plus a process supervisor (`deploy/supervisor.py`) instead of an in-process exec. |
| `commands_user` | ported | `waifu/plugins/collection.py`, `waifu/plugins/economy.py`, `waifu/plugins/gacha.py`, `waifu/plugins/stats.py`, `waifu/plugins/players.py`, `waifu/plugins/misc.py` | 57 functions: collection pages and navigation, ``/daily`` + streaks, ``/spin``, ``/profile`` (incl. glow toggle), ``/help`` keyboard, ``/font``, ``/ping``, ``/search``, ``/top`` with callback paging, ``/sell``/``/gift``/``/give``, shop + claim views, ``check_ban`` (middleware), ``loading_animation`` (chat-action + draft streaming). Inline-mode pieces live in the inline plugin; see ``inline_search``. |
| `config` | adapted | `waifu/settings.py`, `waifu/db/repositories/characters.py`, `.env.example` | Every constant is either a validated ``Settings`` field or a DB row (prices/chances), because in the reference the two could disagree. ``RARITY_DISPLAY`` (the 18 strings) is ``Rarity.display`` in ``waifu/enums.py`` and the two are asserted byte-identical by ``tests/test_uploads.py``. ``ALLOWED_IMAGE_HOSTS`` -> ``ALLOWED_MEDIA_HOSTS``. |
| `database` | adapted | `waifu/db/repositories`, `waifu/db/database.py`, `waifu/db/migrations` | 48 hand-rolled SQL helpers -> typed async repositories over the same tables, with ``INSERT OR REPLACE`` replaced by update-in-place so an upload cannot wipe a description, and the schema owned by migrations. |
| `font` | ported | `waifu/utils/font.py`, `waifu/plugins/misc.py` | MONO/FRAKTUR/SCRIPT/DOUBLE maps and ``/font`` selection, stored per player. |
| `get_emojis` | superseded | `scripts/build_catalogue.py`, `waifu/tg/text.py` | A one-off script that patched a ``log_custom_emojis`` handler into main.py to harvest emoji ids from live traffic. Here the ids are configuration (``waifu/data/emoji_map.json``) and the catalogue build reads them, so nothing has to be spliced into the entry point. |
| `hstats` | ported | `waifu/services/hstats.py` | The stats maths (rarity names, progress bars, item display, md->HTML) behind ``/hstats``/``/hrarity``/``/hcompletion``/``/htop``. |
| `inline_search` | ported | `waifu/plugins/inline.py` | ``inline_search``/``character_result``/``rarity_emoji`` plus the three functions that survive only in the bytecode — ``collection_inline``, ``get_inline_list_result``, ``get_rarity_id`` — i.e. inline roster search *and* 'list my collection' through ``@bot <query>``, with per-result buttons. |
| `main` | adapted | `waifu/core/app.py`, `waifu/core/dp.py`, `waifu/__main__.py` | ``register_handlers``/``post_init``/``error_handler``/``validate_config`` -> ``register_plugins`` + ``command_menu`` in ``waifu/core/dp.py``, the startup hooks in ``waifu/core/app.py`` (menu, identity, capability negotiation) and ``on_error``, which logs with the update attached instead of printing and continuing. The bytecode-only ``init_sudo_db``/``is_owner``/``is_sudo`` are migration-managed tables + ``waifu/core/access.py``. |
| `market` | ported | `waifu/plugins/market.py`, `waifu/plugins/shop.py`, `waifu/plugins/economy.py`, `waifu/plugins/premium.py` | ``market_cmd``/``market_cb``/``rerender_market``, ``buy_item``, ``inv_cmd``/``inv_via_query``, ``pinfo_cmd``, ``hclaim_command``, ``summon``, ``daily``, ``bomb_cmd``/``steal_cmd``/``skip_cmd``, cooldowns, premium checks. Cooldowns are Redis-backed with a DB fallback rather than a column rewritten per call. |
| `media_urls` | ported | `waifu/tg/media.py` | ``is_allowed_character_image_url``/``require_character_image_url`` -> ``is_allowed_image_url``/``require_image_url`` with the same rule set (https, allow-listed host, no userinfo, a real path), and the same refusal used on *both* ingest doors (``/addchar`` and every URL read back out of the roster). |
| `migrate_character_media_to_urls` | superseded | `waifu/services/cards.py`, `waifu/plugins/uploads.py` | The reference's one-way migration *away* from file_ids. This bot runs the useful half in both directions: ``/archiveart <id|missing>`` re-hosts hotlinked art into a permanent file_id, and the host buttons offer the URL back out. No offline script needed. |
| `migrate_sqlite_to_postgres` | ported | `scripts/import_summon.py`, `waifu/__main__.py` | Table-by-table copy with type/name mapping (``characters.id`` text -> integer, ``msg_id`` -> typed columns) -> ``python -m waifu import-legacy <summon.db>``; it reads the same columns and reports what it could not carry instead of guessing. |
| `nguess` | ported | `waifu/plugins/nguess.py`, `waifu/services/spawn.py` | ``nguess_cmd``/``handle_guess``/``new_session``/``nguess_end``/``send_character``/``react_to_message``/``add_coins``/``ensure_user``/``db_query``/``get_random_character``/``get_fresh_character``/``nguess_dm_block``/``async_react`` -> ``/nguess`` with ``/ngpoll``, ``/ngskip``, ``/ngstats``, ``/ngtop``. DM spam is blocked by the same rule (privacy gate), votes are a poll + reaction tally. |
| `profile` | ported | `waifu/services/cards.py`, `waifu/plugins/players.py`, `tests/test_profile_card.py` | ``plugins/profile.py`` (516 lines: gradient canvas, ``draw_glow_rect``, ``draw_rarity_ring``, ``draw_rarity_badge`` with its gold star, ``smart_truncate``, ``progress_bar``) -> ``ProfileArt`` + ``ProfileCardMixin`` + ``/pcard`` (aliases ``/card``, ``/profilecard``). The visual grammar is reproduced at the same 1000x540; what changed is the machinery: fonts are fetched once on demand instead of with blocking ``requests`` at import, the draw runs in a worker thread, the PNG is cached by a signature derived from every field the card prints, the portrait respects the media-host allow list (the reference fetched ``img_url`` blindly), and ``show_balance`` masks the number before rendering so a cached card cannot leak it to the wrong viewer. ``/glow``, ``/bio`` and the ``card_portrait`` flag ride along as prefs. |
| `smoke_test` | superseded | `tests` | Import-and-send smoke checks -> 200-test pytest suite plus ``python -m waifu doctor`` for the live bot. |
| `storage` | adapted | `waifu/db/database.py`, `waifu/db/repositories`, `waifu/settings.py` | The ``?``->``%s`` SQL translator, ``_is_table_info_query``, ``_normalise_value`` and ``using_postgres`` exist only because the reference hand-wrote SQL against two backends; SQLAlchemy removes the class of problem, so the port is 'no equivalent code', and ``configure()``/``connect()`` map onto settings + ``Database.from_settings`` with ``async with db.tx()`` as the savepoint door the middleware uses per update. |
| `supervisor` | ported | `deploy/supervisor.py`, `deploy/summon-bot.service.example`, `docker-compose.yml` | Crash-restart loop with the same AUTO_RESTART_MINUTES default (0 = never recycle on a timer), the same SIGTERM/SIGINT handling and 30s grace for the child. Added: N quick failures in a row stop the supervisor with the child's code, because the reference restarted forever and turned a bad DATABASE_URL into an endless chain of identical tracebacks. deploy/summon-bot.service.example wires it to systemd. |
| `test_bootstrap_postgres` | superseded | `tests/test_catalogue_seed.py` | Reference-side test of the bootstrap guard. |
| `test_storage_savepoints` | superseded | `tests/test_gameplay_flows.py` | Reference-side test of savepoint behaviour in the SQLite/Postgres shim. |

**Totals:** adapted 4 · ported 17 · superseded 7 · tooling 1 across 29 modules.

## Reference database schema (`summon.db`)

The clone ships a real deployment's database. Its rows are not part of this audit
(they are somebody's players); its *shape* is, because that is what a port has to
speak to. Counts show what a working deployment actually holds.

```sql
CREATE TABLE activity_log (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            user_id INTEGER,
            action TEXT,
            timestamp TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
        )  -- TABLE activity_log
CREATE TABLE auction_bid_input (
            user_id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            auction_id  INTEGER NOT NULL,
            created_at  REAL    NOT NULL
        )  -- TABLE auction_bid_input
CREATE TABLE auction_bids (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, auction_id INTEGER, user_id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, created_at DATETIME)  -- TABLE auction_bids
CREATE TABLE auctions (
            id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            character_id    TEXT    NOT NULL,
            seller_id       INTEGER NOT NULL,
            start_price     INTEGER NOT NULL,
            highest_bid     INTEGER NOT NULL,
            highest_bidder_id INTEGER,
            chat_id         INTEGER,
            pinned_msg_id   INTEGER,
            created_at      REAL    NOT NULL,
            end_time        REAL    NOT NULL,
            status          TEXT    DEFAULT 'active'
        )  -- TABLE auctions
CREATE TABLE banned_users (
            user_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            username TEXT
        , reason TEXT)  -- TABLE banned_users
CREATE TABLE characters (
            id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
            name TEXT,
            anime TEXT,
            rarity TEXT,
            msg_id TEXT,
            created_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
        , img_url TEXT, img_url2 TEXT)  -- TABLE characters
CREATE TABLE claim_list (
            rarity_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            chance REAL,
            rarity_name TEXT
        )  -- TABLE claim_list
CREATE TABLE gift_log (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            from_user INTEGER,
            to_user INTEGER,
            char_id TEXT,
            gifted_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
        )  -- TABLE gift_log
CREATE TABLE group_settings (
            chat_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            message_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            spawn_limit INTEGER DEFAULT 100
        )  -- TABLE group_settings
CREATE TABLE groups (
            chat_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY
        , message_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0)  -- TABLE groups
CREATE TABLE market_pool (
            char_id TEXT,
            displayed_at TEXT
        )  -- TABLE market_pool
CREATE TABLE market_transactions (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            user_id INTEGER,
            char_id TEXT,
            transaction_type TEXT,
            price INTEGER,
            timestamp TEXT
        )  -- TABLE market_transactions
CREATE TABLE premium (user_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, expires_at DATETIME, granted_at DATETIME, granted_by INTEGER)  -- TABLE premium
CREATE TABLE rarity_chances (
            rarity_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            rarity_name TEXT,
            chance_value INTEGER
        )  -- TABLE rarity_chances
CREATE TABLE redeem_codes (
            code TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
            character_id TEXT,
            uses INTEGER DEFAULT 1,
            created_by INTEGER,
            reward INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            created_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
        )  -- TABLE redeem_codes
CREATE TABLE sudo_admins (user_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, added_by INTEGER, added_at DATETIME)  -- TABLE sudo_admins
CREATE TABLE sudo_users (
            user_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            username TEXT,
            added_at TEXT
        )  -- TABLE sudo_users
CREATE TABLE user_achievements (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            user_id INTEGER,
            achievement_id TEXT,
            unlocked_at TEXT,
            UNIQUE(user_id, achievement_id)
        )  -- TABLE user_achievements
CREATE TABLE user_collection (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            user_id INTEGER,
            character_id TEXT,
            count INTEGER DEFAULT 1,
            obtained_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
            UNIQUE(user_id, character_id)
        )  -- TABLE user_collection
CREATE TABLE user_inventory (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, user_id INTEGER, item_id TEXT, uses_remaining INTEGER, expires_at DATETIME, purchased_at TEXT)  -- TABLE user_inventory
CREATE TABLE user_preferences (
            user_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            collection_mode TEXT DEFAULT 'anime',
            profile_glow INTEGER DEFAULT 1,
            market_filter TEXT DEFAULT 'all'
        )  -- TABLE user_preferences
CREATE TABLE user_streaks (
            user_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            streak_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            last_streak_date TEXT,
            highest_streak INTEGER DEFAULT 0
        )  -- TABLE user_streaks
CREATE TABLE users (
            user_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            username TEXT,
            balance INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            banned INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            favorite TEXT,
            last_daily TEXT,
            last_hclaim TEXT,
            last_spin TEXT,
            font_pref TEXT DEFAULT 'mono',
            first_name TEXT
        )  -- TABLE users
CREATE TABLE warnings (
            user_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            warn_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            warned_by INTEGER,
            reason TEXT
        , warned_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)  -- TABLE warnings
```
